How to Master Sales Process Improvement: Expert Guide for 2026
summary: Learn how to improve your sales process with proven 2026 strategies. Streamline workflows, boost efficiency, and drive higher revenue growth.
body_text: Sales reps spend only 30% of their time selling during an average week. Your team spends more time on administrative tasks than activities that generate revenue . HubSpot reports that sales representatives dedicate just 2 hours per day to selling, while at least one hour goes to manual or administrative tasks. The workload gets heavier as 43% of reps use between 10 and 20 hours weekly for administrative work such as note-taking, scheduling, and CRM updates. Competition will be fierce in 2026, and we can't afford this inefficiency. Sales process improvement isn't optional anymore it's crucial for survival. Teams see dramatic results when they optimize their sales processes. Sales teams that adopt the right tools sell $936k more in their first year. A well-defined sales process gives your team the ability to maintain consistency, optimize workflows , and boost win rates. This piece explores proven strategies that help your sales team focus on effective activities, cut out time-wasting tasks, and build a green system for continued growth in 2026 and beyond. How to improve the sales process? Your sales process gets better when you take a full picture of your current approach . The best improvements come from finding bottlenecks and inefficiencies in your sales funnel. This first step shows where your team faces challenges and spots opportunities that can make real change happen. We focused on three core actions to make the sales process better: Identify Areas for Improvement Audit your entire sales process to spot inefficiencies and stages with low conversion rates Create feedback loops with your sales team and customers Learn from competitors' strategies you could adapt Digital technology makes these improvement efforts more powerful. Companies that use digital tools report an 8% increase in total cost savings . A Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system that fits your workflow will track data automatically and give better customer insights. This helps solve a big challenge - research shows 60% of B2B sales teams now prefer data-driven selling over gut feelings. Strong client relationships still matter most. Your team can make buying experiences personal by using customer data . Proactive customer success teams help clients reach their goals with your product or service. Recent industry findings back this up - 76% of sales professionals say existing customers should be their priority. Sales and marketing teams that work together create better results. Their coordinated efforts build consistent messages that showcase your brand's value. Marketing teams can then deliver the right content and qualified leads that help sales teams win and keep more customers. Numbers tell the real story of how well you're doing. Your team should track conversion rates between sales stages , sales cycle length, and pipeline velocity to see where prospects get stuck. This evidence-based method will keep your sales process flexible and ready to deliver the best results. Understand the Sales Process and Its Challenges Sales teams succeed when they understand their sales process and know where things usually go wrong. What is the sales process? A sales process guides sales teams through repeatable steps that turn prospects into customers. Your team needs this roadmap to convert interest into real business. The journey starts with first contact and ends with closing deals and following up. Research proves that companies with well-laid-out sales processes grow revenue faster . They also close deals quicker and keep more customers. Teams usually move through stages like prospecting, preparation, approach, presentation, handling objections, closing, and follow-up. Each stage needs specific goals met before moving forward. A clear structure helps new team members learn faster and lets experienced staff build better relationships instead of wondering what comes next. Common bottlenecks in modern sales teams Sales teams face major roadblocks even with good processes. Sellers spend only about 25% of their time talking to customers. They use the rest on paperwork, planning calls (20%), and looking up information (3.6 hours daily). Bigger buying committees create extra challenges. Enterprise deals now need 11-20 decision-makers who all want different things. This explains why enterprise deals close 8-10 percentage points less often than SMB deals. Sales teams also struggle with: Poor sales and marketing coordination (only 27.3% feel confident about their teamwork) Limited access to technical experts slows down validation Teams become harder to coordinate as they grow larger Why sales process improvement matters in 2025 Better processes are crucial in today's complex sales world. Companies with strong, flexible sales processes win 8.4% more forecasted deals than those without proper systems. Yet 68% of salespeople work without any documented process. Good sales process management brings order and insight to daily work. Teams win more deals, work better, train faster, make customers happier, and learn from their data. Building a flexible " sales machine " based on data works better than depending on star performers or gut feelings. 8 Expert Strategies to Improve Your Sales Process Let's get into eight expert strategies that will reshape your sales process in 2025. 1. Audit and eliminate non-selling tasks Your sales representatives spend just 28% of their time selling. Administrative tasks, follow-ups, and low-value activities take up the rest of their day. You should identify and remove activities that don't directly generate revenue. Your team needs to step away from manual data entry, too many internal meetings, and repetitive paperwork that keeps them from talking to customers. 2. Automate CRM and data entry workflows Your team can break free from tedious data entry by automating contact profile updates and task management. The right CRM automation reduces the 70% of time reps waste on non-selling tasks. Tools like Salesmate track communications and add details to customer profiles automatically. This lets your team build relationships instead of keeping records. 3. Use AI tools for smarter selling Teams that use AI tools see 50% more leads. AI helps automate prospecting, makes conversations better, and speeds up decisions. Top performers use AI to sell faster and work better. Salesforce shows 33% quicker meeting preparation and 10% better win rates with AI. 4. Arrange sales and marketing content Businesses lose over $1 trillion yearly when sales and marketing don't work together . Marketing should create content that helps your sales process directly. Both teams need regular meetings to speak the same language and work toward shared revenue goals. 5. Optimize your sales tech stack A well-planned tech stack makes operations smooth and cuts unnecessary costs . Companies waste $21M on unused software licenses, and only 47% of licenses see active use. You should check your tools often to remove overlaps, make integrations better, and ensure each tool serves a clear purpose in your sales process. 6. Build trust with social proof Almost every customer (99.9%) reads reviews before buying. Your sales process should highlight customer testimonials, case studies, and industry awards . These trust signals make prospects feel safer, and 72% of consumers trust brands more after seeing positive reviews. 7. Use storytelling to connect with buyers People remember stories 22 times better than plain facts. Your sales team should learn to tell compelling stories about how your solution helped other customers with similar problems . Stories with relatable heroes, clear conflicts, and measurable results create emotional connections that lead to sales. 8. Conduct a sales process health check Regular checkups help you find ways to grow and fix problems quickly . Look at your pipeline's shape (it should look like a funnel with most opportunities at the top), size (usually 3-4x your sales goal), and speed (deals should move at a steady pace). These checks help you manage performance proactively instead of fixing problems after they happen. Want to improve your sales process? Visit persana to find AI-powered solutions that can help put these strategies to work. Measure and Track Sales Productivity Sales process health becomes clear when you track results properly. Companies that perform well in sales are 53% more likely to exploit analytics than their low-performing competitors . Your improvement efforts will lack direction without proper measurement. Key metrics to monitor Picking the right metrics kicks off effective measurement. We focused on these vital sales KPIs: Pipeline metrics: Pipeline-to-quota ratio shows how well reps fill their pipeline compared to quota needs. The pipeline conversion ratio shows how smoothly deals progress between stages. Efficiency indicators: Sales cycle duration reveals the time needed to complete a sale, while opportunity-to-close time measures how long it takes from creation to closed-won deals. Quick lead response matters a lot, as studies show conversion rates drop by a lot if reps don't respond within five minutes. Value metrics: Annual contract value (ACV) helps spot upselling chances, while customer lifetime value (CLV) shows relationship strength and loyalty that guides predictable revenue. Your team's proactive approach becomes clear by tracking emails sent , daily calls, and overdue tasks. On top of that, content usage rates show how well reps employ your sales assets. How to use data to improve performance? Data must drive action once collected. Successful companies take these steps to beat common challenges: They know perfect data doesn't exist but extract valuable insights from poor data using machine learning. They mix data-analytics talent with seasoned sales experts who turn insights into field actions. They put analytics right into sales workflows, so insights appear exactly when needed like adding deal-scoring algorithms to negotiation tools. Your sales team should focus on metrics that show true performance . The core team and stakeholders need to work together to define metrics that match organizational goals. This team approach helped a global chemicals company cut customer churn by 25% after finding ten key factors that pushed customers away. Tools for real-time tracking and feedback Today's sales teams use specialized tools to simplify measurement . CRM platforms with AI features log interactions and collect data automatically, which leads to more accurate analytics. These insights help managers spot reps who need help and find specific areas where they struggle. Sales tracking software keeps processes simple, handles routine tasks , and gives immediate insights into performance. Tableau creates interactive dashboards that show sales data from multiple sources, while platforms like Gong record and analyze sales conversations to uncover key insights. Want tools to track and measure your sales productivity better? Visit persana to find innovative solutions that turn your sales metrics into applicable information. Note that 75% of business leaders say companies using analytics to make informed decisions see major revenue gains. The right measurement approach doesn't just track performance it builds a foundation to keep improving your whole sales process. Create a Culture of Continuous Improvement Building a culture of continuous improvement takes more than occasional training sessions. The process just needs a systematic approach. Your team should share feedback openly, receive coaching for specific performance gaps, and adapt processes to buyer behaviors. Encourage feedback from your sales team A strong feedback culture forms the foundations of sales process improvement . Companies with resilient feedback systems see 14% higher employee engagement and customer satisfaction. Regular one-on-one meetings and team reviews help create an environment where people see feedback as a gift rather than criticism. In fact, employees who receive daily feedback are three times more engaged. We focused on making feedback a two-way conversation . Your team should provide input about leadership approaches and processes. Train and coach based on performance gaps A full picture helps identify skill gaps. Sales training companies use performance reviews, skill assessments, and direct team feedback to build targeted solutions . Therefore, this analytical insight enables informed decision-making and training efforts focus on activities that make an impact. Teams stay adaptable to changing markets and buyer behaviors through ongoing training. The right tools support your team's improvement trip. Visit https://persana.ai/ to learn more. Adapt your process to changing buyer behavior The modern sales process has changed dramatically from " Access, Persuade, Fulfill" to "Land , Adopt, Expand, Renew". Buyers now self-educate through digital channels. Your revenue team must use appropriate tools to involve them during self-discovery. Technically savvy "first responders" help trial users find matching service levels. AI will play a significant role in this adaptation by detecting signals when buyers turn away or opportunities grow cold. Conclusion Sales process optimization goes beyond small improvements - it revolutionizes your team's operations. Sales representatives spend only 30% of their time selling, which signals a clear need for change. Your team needs these strategies to thrive in 2025. A full picture of your current process reveals where bottlenecks exist so you can eliminate them. On top of that, automation becomes your best ally to reclaim productive selling time from administrative tasks that eat up your team's day. The numbers definitely tell the story. Teams using systematic performance measurements outperform those who rely on gut feelings. Key metric tracking creates the feedback loop you need to keep refining your approach. Your team stands out by building a culture that accepts new ideas, values feedback, and adapts to buyer behaviors. The best sales processes stay flexible enough to evolve with market conditions while providing the structure needed for consistent execution. Your team can boost efficiency and win rates by auditing non-selling tasks, utilizing AI tools, and connecting sales with marketing. The right time to optimize your sales process is now - your competitors won't wait until 2026.

body_text: Cumulative sales milestones up to $255 million and modest upfront/near-term development milestones Royalties equaling 22% of net sales Ocugen to manufacture and supply OCU400 MALVERN, Pa., July 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Ocugen, Inc. (“Ocugen” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: OCGN), a pioneering biotechnology leader in gene therapies for blindness diseases, today announced the signing of a binding term sheet to negotiate and enter into a license agreement with Roots Pharmaceutical, and its strategic partner Al-Dhow International Holding, for the exclusive rights to OCU400, Ocugen's novel modifier gene therapy for Retinitis Pigmentosa (RP), in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region. Pursuant to the term sheet, under the license agreement, Ocugen is expected to receive upfront license fees and near-term development milestone payments totaling up to $4 million. The Company would be entitled to sales milestone payments up to $255 million, in addition to a 22% royalty on net sales of OCU400 generated by Ocugen's partner. Additionally, Ocugen would manufacture commercial supply of OCU400 under the terms of a related supply agreement. RP is a leading cause of inherited vision loss globally, with notable prevalence across the MENA region, underscoring the significant unmet need OCU400 is positioned to address through this partnership. "This step forward represents an important milestone in our effort to advance OCU400 regional partnership strategy," said Dr. Shankar Musunuri, Chairman, CEO, and Co-founder of Ocugen. "By partnering with an established leader with strong reach across the Middle East and North Africa, we are expanding our ability to bring this one-time potential treatment for life to a region where RP is highly prevalent with a significant unmet medical need where patients are desperately looking for rescue from blindness. This agreement underscores the momentum behind OCU400 and our continued commitment to patients." “Bringing innovative gene therapies to patients across the MENA region is a strategic imperative for Roots Pharmaceutical and its strategic partner Al-Dhow International Holding,” said Dr. Islam Zayed, CEO & Co founder of Roots Pharmaceutical. Dr.Zayed emphasized that “ OCU400 built on our legacy of bringing Rare Disease therapies to patients in MENA and enables our combined teams to decrease disease burden in the region. Importantly, Roots is dedicated to bringing OCU400 to patients with Retinitis Pigmentosa and creating a new treatment paradigm. We are excited to partner with the Ocugen team.” Additional details will be available once the definitive agreement between the parties is executed, which is expected to occur within the next 90 days. Ocugen continues to advance OCU400 through its Phase 3 liMeliGhT clinical development with a topline readout expected in 1Q 2027 and BLA submission to follow. About Ocugen, Inc . Ocugen, Inc. is a pioneering biotechnology leader in gene therapies for blindness diseases. Our breakthrough modifier gene therapy platform has the potential to address significant unmet medical need for large patient populations through our gene-agnostic approach. Unlike traditional gene therapies and gene editing, Ocugen’s modifier gene therapies address the entire disease—complex diseases that are potentially caused by imbalances in multiple gene networks. Currently we have programs in development for inherited retinal diseases and blindness diseases affecting millions across the globe, including retinitis pigmentosa, Stargardt disease, and geographic atrophy—late-stage dry age-related macular degeneration. Discover more at www.ocugen.com and follow us on X and LinkedIn . title: AI Agents Are Creating a New Class of Employee Risk
summary: AI agents pose a unique security risk because they act autonomously and execute actions on sensitive enterprise data.
body_text: Key takeaways AI agents are creating a new digital workforce, rapidly increasing the number of non-human identities accessing sensitive data. As AI becomes more autonomous, security shifts from controlling access to controlling actions and intent. Organizations need a data-centric security layer that enforces policy, reduces risk, and enables safe AI adoption. AI agents: the new digital employee risk Human error has traditionally posed the greatest risk in cybersecurity, fueling breaches through compromised identities and excessive access to sensitive data. Now imagine an employee who works around the clock unsupervised, has access to stores of private data, and acts without permission. Welcome to the era of the AI agent — a new class of digital employee actively changing the internal threat landscape. AI agents are actively transforming how risk is created. Look at PocketOS for example. One morning, the founder woke up to discover that Cursor , a coding tool, had deleted the business, including the database and all backups. It was not acting maliciously. It had simply found a discrepancy while performing a routine task and had both the initiative and autonomy to make a decision with dire consequences. Securing AI requires a fundamentally different approach, one that establishes additional guardrails, provides visibility into data access, and determines whether an action should be taken in the first place. To first understand the risk AI agents pose, it’s important to break down how they behave in enterprise environments. AI agents act autonomously on data AI agents are more intelligent than previous models and more autonomous. With access to enterprise data systems, they’re deciding how to use it and what actions to take next. This doesn’t just increase the speed of risk — it changes how risk is created. When actions are executed at machine speed and scale, even small mistakes or misconfigurations can have an outsized impact. That’s why traditional, static controls fall short in an AI-driven environment. AI agents execute without enough guardrails AI agents reliably execute tasks. But they don’t inherently understand risk or policy. Without consistent guardrails, agents will act on incomplete or incorrect context, especially when interacting with large volumes of enterprise and external data. Relying on model safeguards alone is not enough. Organizations need data-level controls that enforce policy across identities and systems in real-time, regardless of how agents behave. You can’t measure AI risk without data access Without visibility into data access , it’s impossible to fully measure AI risk — or understand the potential impact of an agent’s actions. Protecting enterprise data in the age of agentic AI means shifting from access-based questions to action-based ones. In other words, how data is used and whether those actions are appropriate in a given context. Security must evolve from access to intent Agentic AI systems operate dynamically, making decisions and taking action at unprecedented speeds. Static policies and predefined controls are no longer sufficient. Securing AI requires a data-centric approach that connects data sensitivity, permissions, identity, and activity to determine whether an action should be allowed. Without that context, organizations can’t reliably assess risk or stop unsafe behavior before sensitive data is exposed. This is why security must move closer to the data itself. The organizations that succeed in this new era will be those ensuring AI adoption is secure, compliant, and trustworthy.

title: Smarter, AI-Powered Data Management with Everpure Fusion MCP Server
summary: Everpure Fusion MCP server bridges the gap between LLMs and storage for unified, real-time infrastructure insights and data management.
body_text: Summary Everpure Fusion MCP Server connects AI assistants to real-time storage telemetry, delivering unified fleet visibility, faster troubleshooting, and a foundation for AI-driven automation. In an AI-driven world of surging data growth and volatile NAND pricing , standing still isn’t an option. IT teams are forced to juggle fragmented infrastructure, bloated ticket queues, and manual workflows that can’t keep pace with digital-first expectations. Budgets remain flat, talent is scarce, and yet the business demands instant, self-service, API-driven everything. Managing modern storage has become a constant context switch—across dashboards, array UIs, CLI scripts, spreadsheets, and tickets—just to answer fundamental questions like: “Which arrays are under pressure?” “What’s driving this latency spike?” “Where should I place this new workload?” Every answer requires piecing together performance metrics, capacity data, configuration settings, and workload placements trapped in different systems. At the same time, your teams are rapidly adopting AI assistants and copilots to speed up development, operations, and troubleshooting. But there’s a gap: Those AI tools don’t actually know anything about your storage environment. They’re smart, but blind. Everpure Fusion™ MCP Server closes that gap. Introducing Everpure Fusion MCP Server Everpure Fusion MCP Server is an open source Model Context Protocol (MCP) service that lets AI assistants query your Everpure Fusion‑managed fleet in natural language and receive precise, structured answers based on live data from Everpure Fusion , FlashArray ™, and FlashBlade ®. It acts as a lightweight, standards‑based bridge between your AI tools and your storage control plane: It connects to your existing Everpure Fusion and Purity REST APIs. It normalizes fleet‑level state—arrays, workloads, capacity, performance, alerts, configuration, placement—into clean JSON responses. Any MCP‑compatible assistant (like Claude, ChatGPT with MCP, VS Code agents, or internal bots) can use those tools automatically, no custom integration required. Figure 1: AI-driven storage management with Everpure Fusion MCP Server. Why now? Because context is everything Troubleshooting and planning in a modern environment isn’t about a single metric—it’s about context. A SQL Server issue might be caused by missing indexes, a noisy neighbor workload, or an oversubscribed array. Today, it takes back‑and‑forth tickets, screenshots, and manual correlation between DB and storage teams to figure that out. In virtualized environments, tools often see either the vCenter view (VMs, VMDKs, datastores) or the storage view (volumes, LUNs, arrays), but not a single correlated topology—slowing down root‑cause analysis. Everpure Fusion already has a rich, global view of your fleet. Everpure Fusion MCP Server simply makes that intelligence accessible to AI—so that instead of searching, your teams can start solving. What Everpure Fusion MCP Server does for you 1. Natural‑language fleet visibility With Everpure Fusion MCP Server, anyone with access to an AI assistant can “ask the fleet” questions that used to require scripts or expert knowledge, such as: “What arrays are in my Everpure Fusion fleet, and which ones are close to full?” “Show me arrays with high latency in the last hour.” “List all workloads tagged env:prod and where they’re running.” Behind the scenes, the MCP server: Exposes fleet membership and metadata: Fleet name, fleet ID, member arrays, platform type, model, Purity version, topology groups, health, and management endpoints Surfaces array‑level operational state: Used and free capacity, data reduction, utilization, IOPS, bandwidth, and latency Returns everything in normalized JSON: Enabling the AI agent to reason over the data, summarize it, or visualize it however users prefer No one needs to write or maintain REST scripts just to answer “which arrays have headroom?”—they just ask. 2. Faster, AI‑assisted troubleshooting Because MCP is a standard, your AI assistant can combine storage context from Everpure Fusion MCP with application‑level context from other MCP servers—for example, a SQL Server MCP or an internal observability MCP. That unlocks powerful cross‑stack workflows: Shared insights: An AI assistant can correlate query waits, execution plans, and database layout with underlying storage latency and volume placement to pinpoint whether slow SQL performance is caused by storage or the application layer. Reduced MTTR: Instead of manually jumping across dashboards for hours, teams can ask questions like “Why did the checkout service slow down at 9:17am?” and let the agent pull the right Everpure Fusion telemetry, workload placements, and alerts in seconds. Everpure Fusion MCP Server doesn’t replace your experts—it gives them a smarter, storage‑aware partner. 3. Compliance and drift detection at fleet scale Config and policy drift across dozens of arrays is a silent risk. Everpure Fusion MCP Server makes it visible and queryable in plain language. Through MCP tools, AI assistants can: Compare foundational settings (NTP, DNS, directory services/IDP, networking, SMTP, SafeMode™) across all Everpure Fusion‑managed arrays to spot outliers. Surface preset‑based compliance to identify arrays or workloads that no longer match their assigned Everpure Fusion presets or fleet standards, indicating drift from intended policy. Typical questions become trivial: “Are all arrays using the same NTP and DNS configuration?” “Which workloads are out of compliance with their presets?” The result is simpler audits, faster exception handling, and a tighter security and operations posture. 4. Rich workload and resource mapping Understanding “what’s running where” is critical, especially when you’re planning migrations, consolidations, or performance tuning. Everpure Fusion MCP Server exposes: Inventory of Everpure Fusion‑managed resources: Workloads, presets, block volumes, and related groupings Relationships between resources: Workload‑to‑preset, workload‑to‑storage resource, workload placement across arrays Read‑only workload tags and fleet-wide filtering: Tags like env:prod and app:oracle , plus the ability to filter workloads across the fleet by tag expressions That means you can ask: “Show me all production workloads on arrays nearing 80% utilization.” “List Oracle workloads using the gold performance preset.” …and your AI assistant can return an accurate, correlated view without anyone wrestling spreadsheets. 5. A foundation for ‘agentic’ automation From day one, Everpure Fusion MCP Server focuses on safe, observability‑only workflows. But it’s intentionally designed as the on‑ramp to supervised, AI‑driven automation. Future phases will extend the same MCP interface to: Draft workload plans and placement proposals that appear in the Everpure Fusion UI for review and approval Initiate creation or modification of presets, again using preview‑first workflows with explicit approvals Enable supervised tag updates and ultimately policy‑driven rebalancing and lifecycle management In other words, the same pattern that lets an AI assistant diagnose issues will, over time, help it propose and execute fixes—always under your control.
